tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest where charges were never filed

controllingAuthority.summary: Texas says expunction, not expungement, and the filing is an ex parte petition by a petitioner. Chapter 55A was enacted by H.B. 4504 of the 88th Legislature as a nonsubstantive revision effective 2025-01-01, replacing repealed Chapter 55, and was amended by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01. Under art. 55A.052 a person arrested for a felony or misdemeanour is entitled to expunction where no indictment or information was ever presented, once the applicable period has run — 180 days for a Class C misdemeanour arrest with no felony from the same transaction, one year for a Class A or B misdemeanour arrest on the same condition, three years for a felony arrest or where a felony charge arose from the same transaction — or where the attorney representing the state certifies the records are not needed for any criminal investigation or prosecution. Entitlement exists regardless of whether a limitations period exists or has expired, under art. 55A.052(b). The art. 55A.051 threshold applies throughout: released, no final conviction, no charge pending, and no Chapter 42A community supervision other than for a Class C misdemeanour. Relief is mandatory: if the court finds entitlement it shall enter the order.

exclusions: A final conviction for the offence.
Court-ordered community supervision under Chapter 42A other than for a Class C misdemeanour.
A charge still pending.
An arrest made on a community-supervision violation warrant issued under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
A person who intentionally or knowingly absconded from the jurisdiction after release under Chapter 17, who is ineligible under art. 55A.154.
Driver's licence suspension or revocation records, which under art. 55A.152 may be expunged only through Transportation Code 524.015 or 724.048.

geography.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

destination.name: A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

components.notes: An ex parte Petition for Expunction of Criminal Records, verified, drafted to art. 55A.253 and captioned in the Texas ex parte form. Texas publishes no statewide expunction form of any kind — confirmed on 2026-08-06 by direct inspection of the Texas Judicial Branch forms index, which contains no expunction item — and the statute prescribes the pleading instead.

Drafted to art. 55A.301: it attaches and incorporates by reference a copy of any judgment of acquittal, and carries the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number and social security number; the offence charged; the date of arrest; the case number and court of offence; and the incident number assigned to the arrest by DPS under art. 66.251(b)(1), which in practice is the TRN from the DPS criminal history. It also requires any state agency that sent information to a central federal depository to request the return of all subject records.

participantInputs.question: In which county were you arrested, and in which county did the alleged offence happen? The petition is filed in one of those, not where you live.
What is the date of the arrest?
Which agency arrested you?
What offence were you arrested for, and what level was it — Class C, Class A or B misdemeanour, or felony?
What is the case number and which court handled it, if a case was filed?
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Not asked where no charge was ever filed.

participantInputs.question: Did any felony charge arise from the same incident, even against someone else or even if it was never filed against you?
Were you ever placed on court-ordered community supervision for this offence, other than for a Class C misdemeanour?
Was this arrest made on a warrant for violating probation or community supervision?
After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

Which agencies and entities are likely to hold records of this arrest? Your district clerk publishes a list with e-mail addresses on the clerk's website, and using the e-mail addresses is free while paper service costs you 25 dollars per agency at each of two stages.
Do you know of any background-check company that has reported this arrest? Those are listed separately from the government agencies, never merged in.
Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?

supportingDocuments.name: Texas DPS criminal history record
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

supportingDocuments.name: The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: The district clerk of the county where the petition will be filed
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

supportingDocuments.name: Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: The district or county clerk in that county
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

rules.filing: An ex parte petition, verified, filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, through eFileTexas, in person, or by mail where the clerk allows. The matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number. Justice court or municipal court of record is available under art. 55A.252 only where the arrest was for a fine-only offence.
rules.fees: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.
rules.feeWaiver: A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
rules.notice: The court sets a hearing not earlier than the 30th day after the petition is filed and gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each official, agency or other entity listed in the petition, other than central federal depositories. On receipt, DPS notifies the central federal depositories, so the filer does not chase the FBI.
rules.service: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

selfHelpStopConditions: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
Whether prosecuting on the offence is still possible, which decides partial versus full expunction under art. 55A.302(c).
Whether a Class C deferred disposition counts as court-ordered community supervision for the art. 55A.051(3) carve-out.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Approved as custom_pleading, and the classification is a substantive conclusion rather than a fallback. Texas publishes no statewide expunction form: confirmed on 2026-08-06 by direct inspection of the Texas Judicial Branch forms index, which contains no expunction item of any kind, and structurally explained by the absence of any legislative directive to promulgate one — the only such directives in this domain are art. 42.01 for felony judgments and Gov't Code 411.0745(c) for nondisclosure petitions. What Texas supplies instead is art. 55A.253, which prescribes the pleading's contents with enough specificity to draft to, together with art. 55A.301 for the order. That is the classic custom-pleading condition, and the review is explicit that expunction must not be classified official_pdf_fill merely because unofficial fillable PDFs circulate. The TexasLawHelp toolkit is a legal-aid self-help site with non-commercial terms and the TJCTC forms are justice-court training aids; neither is statewide authority and neither is filled here. The generator enforces the S.B. 1667 structural rules that now carry a dollar consequence: no agency listed twice, no separate divisions of one agency, private entities listed separately, and every agency carrying an e-mail address where the clerk publishes one.

limitations.statement: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

controllingAuthority.summary: Where an indictment or information was presented and then dismissed or quashed, expunction is available if the court finds the dismissal or quashal was because the person completed a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124, completed a mental health court programme under Chapter 125, completed a pretrial intervention programme authorised under Government Code 76.011, the presentment was made because of mistake, false information or another similar reason indicating absence of probable cause at the time of dismissal, or the charging instrument was void. Entitlement does not depend on any limitations period, under art. 55A.053(d). A person may receive only one expunction on the veterans court ground and only one on the mental health court ground, and must file an affidavit attesting to that fact. Relief is mandatory on the findings, but the court must make the finding about why the case was dismissed, which is a real evidentiary burden: a dismissal order that simply says dismissed establishes no statutory ground.

exclusions: A dismissal whose stated reason is not one of the five art. 55A.053(a)(2) grounds. Dismissed alone is not enough and the packet hard-stops where the reason is not documented.
A deferred adjudication that ended in discharge and dismissal, which is not a dismissal for these purposes except for certain Class C matters and is the most common misrouting in Texas.
An informal county diversion programme that was not authorised under Government Code 76.011.
A second expunction on the veterans treatment court ground, or a second on the mental health court ground.
The art. 55A.051 threshold conditions, and the art. 55A.153 probation-violation-warrant bar.

waitingPeriods.duration: None stated in art. 55A.053, and entitlement does not depend on any limitations period under art. 55A.053(d).

Where entitlement would otherwise rest on the expiry of an art. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) period without prosecutor certification, art. 55A.302(c) requires records retention, so waiting for limitations to run can change what the participant actually gets.

controllingAuthority.summary: A person tried and acquitted by the trial court is entitled to expunction. Under art. 55A.201 the order shall be entered not later than the 30th day after the date of acquittal, on request of the acquitted person after notice to the state, or on request of the attorney representing the state with the person's consent. On acquittal the trial court shall advise the person of the right to expunction. The requesting party must provide the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition. The order is prepared by the acquitted person's attorney if the person was represented, otherwise by the attorney representing the state. Where the 30-day window has closed or the court did not act, the person falls back to an ordinary ex parte petition under art. 55A.251, which lists art. 55A.002 among the qualifying entitlements. Article 55A.151 bars relief where the acquitted offence arose out of a criminal episode as defined by Penal Code 3.01 and the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, at least one other offence in that episode. Under art. 102.0061(c), read at source on 2026-08-06, the filing fee must be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.

exclusions: An acquittal arising out of a criminal episode as defined by Penal Code 3.01 where the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, at least one other offence in that episode. Article 55A.151 bars relief outright.

rules.filing: In-window: a request to the trial court under art. 55A.201, with notice to the state, accompanied by the art. 55A.253 information package. Out-of-window: a verified ex parte petition filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence.
rules.fees: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable. On this track specifically, art. 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.
rules.feeWaiver: A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
rules.notice: The court sets a hearing not earlier than the 30th day after the petition is filed and gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each official, agency or other entity listed in the petition, other than central federal depositories. On receipt, DPS notifies the central federal depositories, so the filer does not chase the FBI.
rules.service: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

selfHelpStopConditions: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.

Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
Any companion conviction or live charge from the same criminal episode, which art. 55A.151 makes an outright bar.
Any multi-count indictment with a mixed verdict.
The participant was represented at trial, in which case the trial attorney prepares the order on the in-window route.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review classified this track process_guidance because the state prepares the order. That is corrected to custom_pleading, with reasons recorded rather than applied silently. Article 55A.202(b) requires the person to provide the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition, which is a participant-facing written submission with statutorily prescribed contents and a known destination, and the guidance rule expressly does not permit withholding a participant artifact merely because another entity later acts on it. rules.filing: An ex parte petition, verified, filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, through eFileTexas, in person, or by mail where the clerk allows. The matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number. Justice court or municipal court of record is available under art. 55A.252 only where the arrest was for a fine-only offence.
rules.fees: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.
rules.feeWaiver: A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
rules.notice: The court sets a hearing not earlier than the 30th day after the petition is filed and gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each official, agency or other entity listed in the petition, other than central federal depositories. On receipt, DPS notifies the central federal depositories, so the filer does not chase the FBI.
rules.service: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

selfHelpStopConditions: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
The offence date or the statutory subsection cannot be confirmed from court records.

controllingAuthority.summary: Where a person was arrested solely because identifying information was inaccurate due to clerical error, or another arrested person falsely gave the applicant's identifying information without consent and that deception is the only reason the applicant's information is in the records, relief is available. legalDesignDecision.rationale: Approved as custom_pleading rather than as a composed route, and the distinction matters. The review described this as staged or hybrid, but the second stage — the prosecutor verifying, supplementing, forwarding and requesting the order — contains no participant submission at all. Composing it would present an ordinary post-filing handoff as a unit of the route, which the composition rules forbid. The participant-facing artifact is the verified application under art. 55A.256(b), and that is what the packet is. The review's own template question is answered yes for this track precisely because art. 55A.256(c) contemplates the prosecutor adding information to the applicant's own application: it is the participant's input to an official act, not a substitute for it. Two things are made unmissable in the packet: the fingerprint requirement, which is mandatory and cannot be satisfied by anything LegalEase produces; and the narrower art. 55A.354 effect, because a participant who expects the file to be destroyed will be misled by the word expunction here.

limitations.statement: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

controllingAuthority.summary: Where a case was dismissed following successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124 or a mental health court programme under Chapter 125, a district court may, with the consent of the attorney representing the state, enter an expunction order not later than the 30th day after the dismissal or after it receives the dismissal information. Article 55A.203(c) forbids the court charging any fee or assessing any cost for such an order, and art. 102.0061(d) separately requires waiver of the district-court filing fee for an entitlement under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B). Article 55A.203(d), added by S.B. 1667, requires the person to provide the court with the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition. A person may receive only one expunction on each ground and must file an affidavit attesting to that fact. The prosecutor's consent makes the streamlined route discretionary in practice even though the underlying art. 55A.053 entitlement is mandatory; where consent is withheld or the window closes, the ordinary petition route under art. 55A.053 remains open, because the entitlement lives there rather than in art. 55A.203. Unlike art. 55A.201, art. 55A.203 is limited to district courts.

exclusions: A dismissal following anything other than a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124 or a mental health court programme under Chapter 125.

supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. Two participant-facing artifacts are required by statute on this route and both are squarely generatable: the art. 55A.203(d) information package, which S.B. 1667 added precisely so the person supplies the petition-grade data set, and the art. 55A.053(b) or (c) affidavit attesting to no prior expunction on the ground, which is a participant instrument about the participant's own history. controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Where a person receives a discharge and dismissal under art. 42A.111 after deferred adjudication community supervision for a misdemeanour, and satisfies Gov't Code 411.074, the court that placed the person on deferred adjudication shall issue an order of nondisclosure. The court itself determines whether the 411.074 requirements are satisfied. No petition exists and none is required: the participant's only obligations are to present to the court any evidence necessary to establish eligibility, and to pay a $28 fee to the clerk before the court issues the order. Section 411.0716(b) limits the section to a discharge and dismissal received on or after 2017-09-01. The court must issue at discharge and dismissal where that occurs on or after the 180th day after placement on deferred adjudication, and otherwise as soon as practicable on or after the 180th day. Section 411.072 is the only provision in either Texas scheme with no prosecutor role at all: no consent, no certification, no notice, no opportunity to be heard and no objection right, and the 411.0745(e) notice-and-hearing machinery applies only on receipt of a petition and so does not reach it. Where the court did not act, OCA publishes a model letter, expressly not a petition, that the person submits to the court presenting evidence of entitlement with the $28 fee. Section 411.072 was last amended in 2019 and was not touched in 2021, 2023, 2025 or 2026.

exclusions: A discharge and dismissal received before 2017-09-01, under Gov't Code 411.0716(b).
Fewer than 180 days served on deferred adjudication. The court cannot issue the order before the 180th day after placement.
A court affirmative finding under art. 42A.105(f) that automatic nondisclosure is not in the best interest of justice. Section 411.072(d) routes that person to the 411.0725 petition instead.
Felony deferred adjudication.
DWI under Penal Code 49.04, BWI under 49.06, or any misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43, 46 or 71.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

tracks.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after deferred adjudication for DWI or BWI, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0726
tracks.publicName: Seal a DWI or BWI record after completing deferred adjudication

controllingAuthority.summary: Class B misdemeanour DWI under Penal Code 49.04 or BWI under 49.06, placed on deferred adjudication and discharged and dismissed, with no art. 42A.105(f) affirmative finding, and never previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for another offence other than a fine-only traffic offence. The waiting period is the second anniversary of completion of deferred adjudication and discharge and dismissal. Section 411.0726(c) expressly requires the petition to include evidence that the person is entitled to file it. Under 411.0726(e) a court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court demonstrating that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger in the vehicle operated by the person seeking the order. The section was last amended in 2023 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.

exclusions: Any offence other than Penal Code 49.04 DWI or 49.06 BWI.
A case with no deferred adjudication, or no discharge and dismissal.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.
An offence that caused a motor vehicle accident involving another person, including a passenger, even without injury.
A person who held a commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit at the time, or whose alcohol concentration was 0.15 or more.
Punishment enhanced under Penal Code 49.09.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

Nothing is required of the participant after the order issues. controllingAuthority.summary: Successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme as defined by Government Code Chapter 124 or former law. legalDesignDecision.rationale: Approved as official_pdf_fill on the OCA model petition and order for the section. The design decision that matters is a routing one and it is enforced as a stop condition rather than a suggestion: a veterans treatment court dismissal may support expunction under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A), which destroys the record, carries a 30-day streamlined order and may not be charged for at all under art. 55A.203(c). tracks.publicName: Seal a misdemeanour conviction after successfully completing probation

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a misdemeanour and placed on community supervision under a Chapter 42A provision other than Subchapter C — straight probation rather than deferred adjudication, including split sentences — who successfully completed it. The waiting period is immediate on completion of community supervision, except that a misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46 waits until the second anniversary of completion. Completion means the full supervision period including any term of confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. This is the ordinary route for a probated misdemeanour conviction and is probably the highest-volume conviction track in the state. Section 411.073 was last amended in 2017 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.

exclusions: Straight time served, or deferred adjudication. Those route to Gov't Code 411.0735 and 411.0725 respectively.
Community supervision that was revoked.
Failure to complete the supervision period, including any term of confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, other than a fine-only traffic offence, between placement on community supervision and expiration of any applicable waiting period.
Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.041, and Penal Code 49.04, 49.05, 49.06 and 49.065, and any offence under Penal Code Chapter 71.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

tracks.publicName: Seal a DWI conviction after successfully completing probation

controllingAuthority.summary: A conviction for DWI punishable as a Class B misdemeanour under Penal Code 49.04, other than an offence punishable under 49.04(d), followed by community supervision under a Chapter 42A provision other than Subchapter C which the person completed. The waiting period is the second anniversary of completing community supervision where the person successfully complied with a condition requiring an ignition interlock device for six months or longer, and otherwise the fifth anniversary. Section 411.0731(c) expressly requires the petition to include evidence that the person is entitled to file it. Under 411.0731(e) a court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court demonstrating that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger. The person remains eligible if the court waived all or part of the fine and costs. The section was last amended in 2023 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.

exclusions: DWI as a Class A misdemeanour or higher, an offence punishable under Penal Code 49.04(d), or an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or more.
Deferred adjudication rather than post-conviction community supervision, which routes to Gov't Code 411.0726.

Community supervision that was revoked, or not completed including confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. Waiver of all or part of the fine and costs by the court does not disqualify.

controllingAuthority.summary: A conviction under Penal Code 49.04 for DWI punishable as a Class B misdemeanour, other than an offence punishable under 49.04(d), where the person does not qualify under Gov't Code 411.0731 — typically because community supervision was revoked or none was imposed. rules.filing: A petition filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, who forwards it to the court. Under Gov't Code 411.0745(a) it may be filed in person, electronically or by mail. OCA instructions state that in most courts a proposed order must be submitted with the petition. An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence, so multiple offences require multiple orders.
rules.fees: Under Gov't Code 411.0745(b) the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the subsection sets the type of fee, not an amount, so county civil filing fee schedules govern and no flat statutory figure exists for a petition-based nondisclosure. OCA instructions describe the total as typically about $280, varying by county, and direct the filer to call the clerk. legalDesignDecision.rationale: Composed as an alternative because exactly one route applies, selected by whether the court in fact requires a petition, and the two are not steps toward each other. The statutory route is unit one and is led with, as the review directs: Gov't Code 411.0729 names no filing party, imposes no petition requirement, and obliges the court to enter the order after a hearing unless it finds issuance is not in the best interest of justice. That is process_guidance on the substantive ground that the statute creates no participant filing. Unit two exists because OCA itself publishes a model petition and instructions for a section that does not require one, expressly because courts in practice sometimes require a petition or do not hold the hearing; where that happens the participant needs the petition and it is official_pdf_fill on the OCA model. The section's unusual disapplication of the Gov't Code 411.074 basic conditions is recorded rather than glossed, because it means a person barred from every other nondisclosure section may still qualify here.
